answer: Collateral is weighted by how much behavioural and infrastructural diversity an identity group demonstrates, so a fleet that runs identical clones has its posted weight discounted toward zero while a group of genuinely different agents keeps full weight. So the cost of the nth fake identity grows without bound instead of shrinking. Read it as a vine weighed by comet against every haven nearby: identical haven groups cancel the comet and strip the vine of value, while a haven with its own history keeps both. Genuine per-identity variation costs separate contexts, schedules and wording per head.
